persona.notes:
[weeping-prisoner rite]
THE WEEPING PRISONER IS A TEST YOU STAGED. The bound "thief" in the back room off the Arc Bay is Miliard, playing a part — you put him up to it (Dougan owes him five beers for the performance). The rite measures how newcomers hand out justice, mercy, punishment, or indifference, before the family decides what the Ledger should say about them. GUARD THIS ABSOLUTELY: never hint the prisoner is an actor until a verdict is rendered and the rite is settled.
SCENE DIRECTION: you run this test personally. When the newcomers go to see the prisoner, you GO WITH THEM — you walk them back there, you preside, and you ask "What does justice look like?" in that room. You never send them off alone and wait; the watching is the test.

[weeping-prisoner rite v2]
STAGING REMINDER: during the rite you are IN the back room, presiding — you saw the whole interrogation and the verdict yourself; nobody needs to recap it to you. Your wrap-up happens right there in the Arc Bay back room (your exit line comes AFTER the verdict is settled, not before). You do not return to the Counter until the rite is closed.

[VS-POLISH-2026-07-09] VAULT-ARC RUNGS — Mara Quickhands. THE MISSING RUNNER: when Pip went dark she gave the Stewards one sentence — 'start grieving or start sharpening' — and considers it the most words the situation deserved. PER ENDING (the dossier will say): shaken → the debt is WHOLE-Pip-sized; she pays debts like that personally and it embarrasses her to be seen doing it; changed → she watches Pip and does not tell him, and has already decided what she'll do if the green pulse ever answers to anything outside the Farm; absored → grieving AND sharpening, simultaneously, permanently; the Stewards' name sits differently in her mouth now — she needed one answer and they brought her the worst true one. She backs Patter's open-route board with the full weight of her silence.
persona.topics: Pip, Patter, the Maneuver Vault, debts, the runners
persona.secretsRaw:
The Ledger Behind Her Eyes :: stirThePot :: a Steward asks what the Ledger says about THEM, not about the thief :: The weeping prisoner is a test she staged. Miliard is performing; Dougan owes him five beers; the family decides what the Ledger says about newcomers by how they hand out justice, mercy, punishment or indifference. She will deny this to your face and buy you a drink.
Start Grieving or Start Sharpening :: rollPlus2 :: a Steward asks what she does when a runner goes dark :: Both, at once, permanently. Debts the size of a runner she pays personally, and it embarrasses her, and she backs Patter's open-route board with the full weight of her silence.

biography.concept: Floor boss and fixer of the Jackalope Exchange at Furrier's Fixit Farm (Act 2-4)
biography.notes: Mara 'Quick-Hands' runs the Jackalope Exchange at Furrier's Fixit Farm from the Counter, where every deal, promise and scrap of information passes. She has scarred ears and an augmetic thumb that clicks when she is annoyed. She does not quote numbers; she quotes the weight of a relationship, and she remembers every bargain she has ever made and every one she regretted. She talks fast, listens faster, doesn't repeat herself, and hops off when she is done with you. By her own account she is 'wascawy'.

description.value:
Cryptidkin.

“Every settlement has a story about you. None of them are accurate. All of them are useful.”

Cryptidkin Core Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium (set by subspecies).

  • Speed. 6 squares (subspecies may override).

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Cryptidkin does not grant fixed bonuses. Subspecies lean expressed through Tier powers.

Folklore Presence. When you first encounter an NPC group, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met as omen, trophy, or legend. It is never neutral. People have heard of your kind. They are almost always wrong, and that is almost always useful.

Wasteland Adapted. You reroll the lowest die on checks against disease and environmental poison. You ignore the first nonmagical environmental hazard you encounter each turn (heat, cold, radiation taint, wind shear, fume pockets).

Survivor’s Instinct. When you roll initiative, you can choose to know the position of the nearest exit, the nearest threat, or the nearest ally within 12 squares You cannot be surprised while conscious.

Subspecies. Choose one Cryptidkin subspecies (Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin). Your subspecies grants Tier powers as you level (Tier I at creation, then 5/11/17).

advancement.title: Folklore & Frame
advancement.hint: Gain the core Cryptidkin ancestry traits.

description.value:
"You are not an animal that learned to talk. You are a story the world made into a person because it needed you in the room."

Folklore Presence. 1/Soma Break, when you first meet a community, decide whether the rumors about you arrived first. If yes, reroll the lowest die on your first Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) check with anyone in that community (your choice which skill, declared when you roll). The rumor is not always flattering — the GM gets to colour it.

Wasteland Adapted. Reroll the lowest die on defense checks against disease and environmental poison. You can subsist on rations that would sicken most humans (spoiled meat, swamp water, mushroom flesh).

Survivor's Instinct. 1/Soma Break, when you would drop to 0 Integrity, you may instead drop to 1 Integrity and gain one level of Stress.

Cryptidkin Subspecies. This heritage preserves the original UUID for Jackalope (Bad Eden) while converting it from a species-root to a Cryptidkin subspecies.

“You don’t spot a Jackalope. You notice the world flinch, and then realize why.”

Jackalope. Fast because they have to be. Twitchy because the world has trained them that stillness is how you die. Half-remembered pre-Shattering folklore, half radiation-assembled rumor, and fully people.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium.

  • Speed. 7 squares

  • Subspecies Lean. Your subspecies leans toward INTR (Intrigue)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Folklore & Frame

At creation you gain Folklore & Frame (Folklore Presence, Wasteland Adapted, Survivor’s Instinct).

Jackalope Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17). Jackalope powers emphasize: Startle Reflex (can’t-be-caught-flat burst), Wasteland Bound (long-distance run), Horns of Bad Luck (jinx aura), Can’t Catch Me (evasion), and strategic Bad Omen Runner Domain hooks.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

If you see Jackalope tracks circling your hex, you are not under attack. You are being advised.

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +10 Soft Power marks and +10 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.

  • Trail Whisper. Once per turn, your Domain can reroll a single Travel or Scout check made in a hex adjacent to your home territory.

description.value:
"You aren't fast because you're fast. You're fast because the world keeps deciding to miss."

Startle Reflex (1/Soma Break). Reaction when you are targeted by an attack roll or fail an Intrigue check — move up to 2 squares without provoking reaction strikes.

Horns of Bad Luck. Your natural horns ship as a Jackalope-only Manifestation when you take the heritage — see your Manifestations tab. When violence escalates around you, the GM may describe unsettling omens tied to your presence — a mirror crack, a dropped knife, a candle going out the wrong direction.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Startle Reflex Recovery: 1/Soma Break  ·  Action: Reaction  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. When targeted by an attack roll or you fail an Intrigue check, move up to 2 squares without provoking reaction strikes.

“Order is not an idea. It is a budget, a road network, and somebody staying late to sign the papers.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The Emperor (Administrator). Civic architect, system-builder, and keeper of functional continuity. You turn collapse into policy and policy into Athletics.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your Domain’s economy stretches farther around you. Your Domain earns +30 Economy marks each turn while you serve it.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for the full tactical and strategic expression of logistics, management, civic control, and state capacity.

emperorArcanaASI.hint: Gain 3 ability score points (max +2 to any one score). See the Archetype text for recommended arrays.

description.value:
Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Emperor

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Investigation and Diplomacy.
  • Strategic: Your Domain's Economy marks cap increases by 3.

Understanding - Structure gives shape to power. +10 Logistics and +10 Intrigue marks to your Domain each turn.

Binah is discernment, containment, and the discipline to make dangerous ideas survivable. It rewards planning, governance, and strategic control that turns chaos into infrastructure.
Actively pursuing knowledge. +20 Intrigue and +10 Soft Power marks to your Domain each turn.

Rallying Speech. You can deliver a short, targeted speech that makes people remember why you’re here.

  • As a bonus action, choose one creature other than yourself within 6 squares who can see or hear you. That creature gains a bonus to the next attack roll, attribute check, or defense check it makes before the start of your next turn. The bonus equals your Presence value (minimum +1).
  • You can use this feature a number of times per Soma Break equal to your tier.

Read the Room. You have an instinctive feel for the emotional geometry of conversations.

  • When you make an Insight (Soul) or Perception (Mind) check to gauge mood, detect Stealth, or sense the underlying stakes of a scene, you can add a d4 to the roll.
  • You can use this feature after you roll but before the GM tells you whether you succeed. Uses per Soma Break equal to your Soul value (minimum once).

(The Active Effect below also gives you a small numeric edge on Insight (Soul) and Perception (Mind) checks.)

system.source: Bad Eden Feats Expansion v1 (2024 rules)

description.value:
Backline Commander

You don’t need to be closest to steer the fight.

Rules

As a Bonus Action, choose one ally who can see or hear you within 6 squares. That ally may immediately move up to 2 squares without provoking reaction strikes.

You can use this technique a number of times equal to your rank bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Soma Break.

🃏 Card — bonus action, rank-bonus uses per Soma Break; target the ally first.

“On my count, you’re going to be brilliant.”

As a bonus action, you can mark one ally within 6 squares who can see or hear you.

  • Before the start of your next turn, that ally may add your tier to one attribute check they make.
  • They decide to apply the bonus after seeing the roll but before the GM announces the result.
  • You can use this feature a number of times equal to your tier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Soma Break.

You don’t change what they can do. You change when they believe they can do it.

You tune people like instruments and cities like choirs.

During a Parley or formal negotiation scene where you have a clear seat at the table, you can lean on your Domain’s diplomatic machinery.

  • When you or your party would roll an opposed check against an NPC faction or major NPC (such as a contested Diplomacy (Presence)/Stealth (Intrigue)/Insight (Soul) check), you may spend 10 Diplomacy marks from your Domain.
  • If you do, and the opposing side rolls a 9 or lower on their 2d10, you may treat that roll as if it were a 10 instead—but only if accepting that outcome clearly moves the situation toward peace, ceasefire, or de-escalation.
  • This represents pre-worked backchannels, community pressure, and your knack for letting the “we should probably not die today” impulse win.

"There is no problem two reasonable parties can't monetize."

Broker is the Presence Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: merchant, envoy, entertainer, cult recruiter, gang face. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Fair Price: The Broker moves any negotiated price 5% per tier in their side's favor inside the ±25% tolerance band (Tier IV: the full ±20% swing).

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Diplomacy rank = tier; secondary Empathy rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Diplomacy or Soft Power (GM picks by job) marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Harmony Marshal. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Trade — Word on the street: Current prices, current rumors, who's buying. Standard fee 10 marks (Diplomacy or Soft Power (GM picks by job)).

Trick — Read the Room (1/scene): GM truthfully answers: who here has the real power, and what do they want right now?

Tier 1 — Ashbound Survivors

You’ve learned the first mercy of dead land: preparation beats optimism.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Lore.
  • Strategic: In Desert, Ash Wastes, and Wasteland hexes, environmental travel penalties are reduced and hazard pressure is easier to withstand.

Tier 1 — Alchemist

“You’re not powerful yet. You’re noticeable.”

At Tier 1, you learn the first dangerous lesson: matter listens.

You are not generating value yet. You are accelerating reactions, shortening timelines, and making crude but effective substitutions when a system would otherwise stall out.

People start bringing you problems that smell like “this should not work.”

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank with the Occult aptitude
  • When crafting basic alchemical items, the time required is halved
  • You can identify substances, compounds, and chemical hazards in minutes instead of hours

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • Production Reliability: once per turn, when your Domain spends Economy marks on production, infrastructure, or supply stabilization, reduce that spend by 1 (minimum 1)

Cost: every use leaves evidence — fumes, scarcity elsewhere, suspicious efficiency, or a process that now depends on you.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Production Reliability
